item.content:encoded:
For the last two seasons, Garrett Whitlock has been one of the best pitchers the Boston Red Sox's bullpen has to offer. But the righty has considered changing that.
Whitlock told Tim Healey of The Boston Globe that he would consider a return to life as a starting pitcher (subscription required). Whitlock in 2021 debuted with Boston as a reliever, but he began starting some games shortly after in 2022. He made four starts in 2024 and planned to take his full season as a starter, but a UCL injury derailed that plan.
“I definitely know my body better and know everything better now, and so it’s definitely something I’d be open to," Whitlock said, via Healey. "So it’s one of those things where the team would have to be on board with it and just talk through everything and go through it. But it’s something I’d always be open to.”
Some fans and people in the Red Sox organization could be excited to hear Whitlock say he's interested in reprising his role as a starting pitcher. Boston has just one righty starter in its rotation this year, Sonny Gray, and he'll be a free agent at the end of the season, barring an unexpected contract extension. Whitlock's success in the bullpen could translate to more in the rotation and he could compete for Gray's former spot.
Red Sox should keep Garrett Whitlock in bullpen despite his willingness to return to a starting role
But Whitlock's history as a starter isn't as clean as it is from the bullpen. Whitlock went on the injured list twice in the 2022-23 seasons with hip and elbow issues. He missed all but four appearances of the 2024 season after he underwent the internal brace procedure to repair his UCL. His elbow even flared up after a period of heavy use out of the bullpen this season. Adding starts into his repertoire hasn't worked before, and though it could work now since Whitlock said he's more in-tune with his body, it isn't a risk the Sox should be willing to take.
Whitlock has had more success as a reliever than as a starter, though he's pitched far more in relief and the sample sizes are far from equal. The veteran has posted a 4.29 ERA over 109 innings across 23 appearances as a starter and a 2.37 ERA over 254.1 frames in relief. The Red Sox need right-handed rotation depth, but they also have Tanner Houck, Kutter Crawford and Johan Oviedo recovering from injury, and none of them have established themselves in another role as seamlessly as Whitlock has.
Whitock told Healey that he would return to a starting role if the Red Sox want him to (he's under team control until after the 2028 season due to two club options) or if any new team he signs with wants him to change. For now and in 2027, the Red Sox should stick with the good thing they have, which is Whitlock as one of the most dangerous relievers in the league.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox could have a slew of pitching reinforcements returning before the playoffs begin, including Tanner Houck, Garrett Crochet, and maybe even Johan Oviedo and Kutter Crawford. Justin Slaten will not be among them.
Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy on September 15 told reporters (including Tim Healey of The Boston Globe) that Slaten got a PRP injection in his arm to address a flexor issue. His season is over after multiple attempts to ramp up for a rehab assignment and eventual return.
Slaten has been quite injury prone over his three years with the Red Sox. He went on the injured list for the first time this season in early April and didn't return until mid-May. For the second straight year, he'll finish his season with less than 35 innings pitched.
Justin Slaten's season with Red Sox ends after he gets PCP injection for flexor injury
The righty has dabbled in the extremes this season, finishing with a 4.60 ERA over 31.1 innings. In June, Slaten's worst month this year, he allowed nine runs on 17 hits over 11 outings. July was his best, during which he let up just one run on five hits over nine appearances. His WHIP has starkly increased over the past year, from 1.09 in 2025 to 1.37.
When the Red Sox can get Slaten's best, he's one of the biggest threats out of their bullpen. But he's often injured or prone to blowups that keep him from showing the best he can offer. It will be interesting to see his role next season when Boston has more healthy pitching depth it could push to the bullpen.
Red Sox confirm Kristian Campbell's season is over due to foot injury, ending breakout
Kristian Campbell's season has also ended prematurely due to an injury. The outfielder will be out for the rest of the year due to a left foot contusion, according to Tommy Cassell of the Worcester Telegram & Gazette.
The WooSox pulled Campbell from their September 8 game due to the injury. Even before the announcement of his IL stint, it was evident that Campbell's season could be over, as Worcester's last regular season game is on Septembet 20.
Campbell's injury ends a resurgent second half for the 24 year old. He slashed .311/.430/.497 over 51 games after the All-Star break and, had he been healthy, he might've been selected to come up and help the major league team while Ceddanne Rafaela and Eli White are injured.
Romy Gonzalez continues tear following arm injury scare with WooSox
On the same day Campbell was pulled from the WooSox's lineup, Romy Gonzalez was, too. An arm injury led to a week on the shelf for the utility infielder, but he joined the Triple-A lineup again on September 15.
Gonzalez has resumed the tear he was on before his arm flared up. He logged two hits, including a double, in his return and boosted his September slash line to .500/.520/.727 over six games. Gonzalez has hit so well lately that it could be time to call him back up to the major leagues to give Boston's slumping offense a boost.

item.content:encoded:
Over the last few weeks, the Boston Red Sox have gotten positive updates left and right about injured starting pitchers.
First and foremost, Garrett Crochet has been throwing and is trending towards a late-season return in Boston's bullpen, barring a setback. Tanner Houck has been on a minor league rehab assignment and is trending up. Plus, the current expectation is that Johan Oviedo is nearing a minor league rehab assignment as well. Now, it sounds like another hurler is trending up as well. On Tuesday, Tommy Cassell of the Worcester T&G Sports reported that there have been "some rumblings" that Kutter Crawford could join Triple-A Worcester throughout the week as well.
"And there are some rumblings that Kutter Crawford could be in Worcester this week, too," Cassell wrote. "The 30-year-old righty has been sidelined since March with right wrist and forearm issues and made one rehab stint with Worcester on April 11 before being shut down again. Crawford hasn’t been confirmed yet whether he will pitch in Worcester."
Kutter Crawford Is Trending Up
How about that?
Crawford hasn't been talked about in a long time. Now, it seems like the righty could potentially be in Worcester this week. Things move quickly in baseball, to say the least.
Crawford missed the entire 2025 season and he was trending up at one point early in the 2026 season and even went on a rehab assignment with Triple-A Worcester, although he suffered a setback and has been on the shelf ever since.
Now, of course, this doesn't guarantee that he will help the Red Sox before the 2026 season comes to a close. In fact, it arguably would be surprising to see him on the Red Sox's roster before the season comes to a close. Crawford's last appearance in a game was on April 11, 2026 with Worcester. When he does take the mound again, he's going to have to build up and get the rust off. The regular season will end for the Red Sox in just 12 days, as of writing, on Sep. 27. That's not a lot of time to begin a rehab assignment for the first time in five months and return to the majors with the playoffs looming.
But it's still good news in general for Boston. What if Crawford does pitch this week for Triple-A Worcester and looks like a game-changer? Maybe, he could surprise. Even if he doesn't, he's under team control for the 2027 and 2028 seasons. If the Red Sox could enter Spring Training with Crawford as a legit candidte for either the rotation — or even the bullpen — that makes the team better. Or, if he proves he's healthy, maybe he could even be an intriguing trade chip this winter.
All in all, hearing that one of the Red Sox's hurlers are trending up after missing so much time is positive in itself.
